weeks.intro: Race week. The work is banked — nothing you do now makes you fitter, plenty can make you tired. Short, sharp, rested.

rationale: VO2max 53.4 and a resting HR of 51 put the aerobic engine well ahead of the running volume behind it (13.5 km/week recently) — the Base phase is sized to grow mileage before asking for pace. Fitness 2.0 flags 'grey-zone training' as the top limiter (16% true easy vs. 51% moderate, driven by HYROX cross-training at 120-148 bpm most days) and a habitual fast-start fade in race history (positive-split ratio 1.027) — this plan leans on progressive and race-pace long runs specifically to retrain that pacing pattern, and keeps quality days genuinely hard so the easy days can afford to be genuinely easy.
tips: Guard the easy days — HYROX cardio already supplies plenty of moderate-intensity work; running easy at true conversational effort is where this plan's biggest gap gets closed.
Cadence on recent runs averages 155-160 spm; use every stride/speed session (cadence targets of 172-174 are built into the Peak-phase speed and VO2max sessions) to nudge it up.
Practice negative splits deliberately in the progressive and race-pace sessions — race history shows a fast-start/fade pattern (ratio 1.027) that these sessions exist to correct.
Log RPE on the HYROX cross-training sessions — most are unrated, and they're the only way that load gets counted alongside the running plan.
If training_readiness or HRV drop into clearly low territory close to a hard day, take the easy option — current readiness (47, Garmin status Recovery) is worth watching week to week.
